pillar:C1.why: Reduces raw EEG waveforms to a 24-dimension feature set for quantum feature extraction. Partial: it does not match a qubit register.
pillar:C1.quote: Our approach used a spatial-temporal deep learning architecture to reduce the raw waveforms to a 24-dimension feature set for digitized counterdiabatic quantum feature extraction

pillar:C1.why: A hybrid network with quantum layers in EEGNet, a classical EEG front end. Partial: it does not state compression to qubits.
pillar:C1.quote: a hybrid neural network incorporating quantum layers into EEGNet

pillar:C2.why: Proves that re-uploading models output functions with vanishing high-frequency components.
pillar:C2.quote: we prove that quantum re-uploading models output functions with vanishing high-frequency components and upper-bounded derivatives with respect to data

pillar:C2.why: Maximal expressive power of a re-uploading network grows with depth and qubits but is bounded by the data encoding.
pillar:C2.quote: While the maximal expressive power increases with the depth of the network and the number of qubits, it is fundamentally bounded by the data encoding mechanism

pillar:C3.why: Extracts features of EEG networks with two gradient-based techniques, saliency and GradCam.
pillar:C3.quote: We then extracted and visualized learned features with two gradient-based techniques: saliency and gradient-weighted activation maps (GradCam)

pillar:C3.why: Grad-CAM identifies the EEG channels that contribute to an ADHD diagnosis.
pillar:C3.quote: Grad-CAM also identified significant channels that contributed to the diagnosis outcome

hypothesis:E1.why: Indirect: a single-qubit processor hosts a universal classifier by re-uploading. It does not compare with single-shot encoding.
hypothesis:E1.quote: a single-qubit processor can host a universal classifier based on the re-uploading scheme

hypothesis:E1.why: Indirect: states data re-uploading is necessary for an expressive model. No direct comparison on a classification task.
hypothesis:E1.quote: the data reuploading, which repeatedly encode classical data into quantum circuit, is necessary for obtaining the expressive quantum machine learning model

hypothesis:E2.why: Shows experimentally that a complex ansatz connectivity helps explore wider solution sets but adds transpilation gate overhead.
hypothesis:E2.quote: it is here experimentally shown that a complex connectivity in the ansatz, albeit being beneficial for exploring wider sets of solutions, introduces an overhead of gates during the transpilation

hypothesis:E2.why: Partial: Ring-topology circuits reach the highest entanglement and expressibility, ahead of Linear; not task performance.
hypothesis:E2.quote: circuits following a Ring topology will have the highest entanglement and expressibility values, followed by Linear/All-to-all almost together and the Star topology

hypothesis:E3.why: Proves bounds on gradient differences between data-less circuits and re-uploading models.
hypothesis:E3.quote: We prove bounds for the differences between gradients of the better-studied data-less parameterized quantum circuits and re-uploading models

hypothesis:E3.why: Maximal expressive power increases with network depth yet is bounded by the data encoding mechanism.
hypothesis:E3.quote: While the maximal expressive power increases with the depth of the network and the number of qubits, it is fundamentally bounded by the data encoding mechanism

hypothesis:E4.why: Partial: SHAP attribution, not gradient saliency, finds the largest contributions at frontal and central electrodes.
hypothesis:E4.quote: Post-hoc SHAP attribution identified the highest relative contributions in frontal (F3, Fz, F4) and central (Cz) electrodes

hypothesis:E4.why: Partial: frontal and fronto-central channels show the greatest model-derived contribution, without gradient saliency.
hypothesis:E4.quote: Frontal and fronto-central channels, particularly Fz, showed the greatest model-derived contribution

hypothesis:E4.why: Reports an elevated theta to beta power ratio in children with ADHD.
hypothesis:E4.quote: an elevated power ratio between theta and beta (theta/beta ratio, TBR)

hypothesis:E5.why: Compares how well popular ansatz learn one-dimensional truncated Fourier series.
hypothesis:E5.quote: comparing how well popular ansatz for PQCs learn different one-dimensional truncated Fourier series

hypothesis:E5.why: Reads a large class of PQC models as Fourier series whose frequencies derive from the encoding gates, the basis of the frequency-two rule.
hypothesis:E5.quote: A large class of these models, seen as Fourier series whose frequencies are derived from the encoding gates

layer:Layer 1: EEG inputs.why: Uses a dataset of 121 participants (61 ADHD, 60 controls), the labeled subjects this layer takes as input.
layer:Layer 1: EEG inputs.quote: The model was trained and validated on a dataset of 121 participants (61 ADHD, 60 Healthy Controls)

layer:Layer 1: EEG inputs.why: The public dataset of 121 participants has 19-channel EEG recordings, the C = 19 channels of this layer.
layer:Layer 1: EEG inputs.quote: The public dataset comprised 121 participants (61 ADHD and 60 controls), with 19-channel EEG recordings sampled at 128 Hz

layer:Layer 1: EEG inputs.why: Uses raw EEG from 61 individuals with ADHD and 60 controls during a visual attention task.
layer:Layer 1: EEG inputs.quote: raw EEG recordings from 61 individuals with ADHD and 60 control subjects during a visual attention task

layer:Layer 2: Classical spatial-tempora.why: Compact convolutional EEG network encapsulating known feature-extraction concepts, the reference for a convolutional encoder.
layer:Layer 2: Classical spatial-tempora.quote: We introduce the use of depthwise and separable convolutions to construct an EEG-specific model which encapsulates well-known EEG feature extraction concepts for BCI

layer:Layer 2: Classical spatial-tempora.why: Pre-processes data with a classical network and embeds a select set of informative features into a quantum processor.
layer:Layer 2: Classical spatial-tempora.quote: to optimally pre-process high dimensional data (e.g., images) with any state-of-the-art classical network and to embed a select set of highly informative features into a quantum processor

layer:Layer 2: Classical spatial-tempora.why: Pairs a pretrained EEG encoder with a quantum classifier. Its encoder is pretrained, unlike this one.
layer:Layer 2: Classical spatial-tempora.quote: a hybrid framework combining a large-scale pretrained EEG encoder (DIVER-1) with a differentiable quantum classifier

layer:Layer 3: Circular DRU quantum circ.why: Extends data re-uploading to several qubits, where entanglement expands the superpositions, the multi-qubit circuit of this layer.
layer:Layer 3: Circular DRU quantum circ.quote: The extension of this idea to several qubits enhances the efficiency of the strategy as entanglement expands the superpositions carried along with the classification

layer:Layer 3: Circular DRU quantum circ.why: Repeating simple encoding gates gives access to richer frequency spectra, the expressivity this layer relies on.
layer:Layer 3: Circular DRU quantum circ.quote: By repeating simple data encoding gates multiple times, quantum models can access increasingly rich frequency spectra

layer:Layer 3: Circular DRU quantum circ.why: Ring-topology circuits reach the highest entanglement and expressibility, the closed ring of this layer.
layer:Layer 3: Circular DRU quantum circ.quote: circuits following a Ring topology will have the highest entanglement and expressibility values, followed by Linear/All-to-all almost together and the Star topology

layer:Layer 4: Readout and objective.why: A variational circuit is trained by measuring the expectation value of an operator, the quantity read out here.
layer:Layer 4: Readout and objective.quote: Variational quantum computing schemes train a loss function by sending an initial state through a parametrized quantum circuit, and measuring the expectation value of some operator

layer:Layer 4: Readout and objective.why: Names local readouts of the individual qubits, the per-qubit readout here, and finds them weaker than global-entangling measurements.
layer:Layer 4: Readout and objective.quote: Global-entangling measurements on the network can saturate the maximal expressive bound leading to an enhancement of the approximation capabilities of the network compared to local readouts of the individual qubits in non-entangling networks

layer:Layer 4: Readout and objective.why: Trains an ADHD EEG network with a regularized cross-entropy loss. Subject weighting is this proposal's own choice.
layer:Layer 4: Readout and objective.quote: a cross-entropy loss regularized through α-Rényi mutual information

layer:Layer 5: Clinical interpretability.why: Visualizes a trained EEG network in three ways to interpret its learned features, a classical precedent for reading an EEG model.
layer:Layer 5: Clinical interpretability.quote: We demonstrate three different approaches to visualize the contents of a trained EEGNet model to enable interpretation of the learned features

layer:Layer 5: Clinical interpretability.why: Analyzes a trained ADHD model to identify key brain regions and frequency bands, the biomarker reading contrasted post hoc.
layer:Layer 5: Clinical interpretability.quote: To clarify model explainability and identify key brain regions and frequency bands for ADHD diagnosis, we analyzed the learned weights and activation patterns of the model's primary layers

layer:Layer 5: Clinical interpretability.why: Visualizes a classifier from the gradient of the class score with respect to the input. Stated for images, not EEG.
layer:Layer 5: Clinical interpretability.quote: We consider two visualisation techniques, based on computing the gradient of the class score with respect to the input image

layer:Layer 5: Clinical interpretability.why: Gradients of expectation values come, in many instances, from running the circuit twice with one gate parameter shifted, the quantum factor of the saliency.
layer:Layer 5: Clinical interpretability.quote: in many important instances it is sufficient to run the original quantum circuit twice while shifting a single gate parameter to obtain the corresponding component of the gradient

layer:Layer 5: Clinical interpretability.why: Excessive Theta/Beta ratio is not a reliable diagnostic measure of ADHD, which bounds how far a Theta/Beta contrast may be read.
layer:Layer 5: Clinical interpretability.quote: Excessive TBR cannot be considered a reliable diagnostic measure of ADHD, however a substantial sub-group of ADHD patients do deviate on this measure

equation:1.why: Embeds a select set of informative classical features into a quantum processor, the map to d = N_q features. It does not state the tanh bound.
equation:1.quote: to embed a select set of highly informative features into a quantum processor

equation:1.why: A spatial-temporal network reduces raw EEG to a small feature set for quantum feature extraction, the role of f_phi. Its size is 24, not 4.
equation:1.quote: Our approach used a spatial-temporal deep learning architecture to reduce the raw waveforms to a 24-dimension feature set for digitized counterdiabatic quantum feature extraction

equation:2.why: Organizes the circuit as a series of data re-uploading and processing units, the layered product of this equation.
equation:2.quote: A quantum circuit can then be organized as a series of data re-uploading and single-qubit processing units

equation:2.why: Studies data re-uploading models built from repeated encoding layers, the layered structure of this product.
equation:2.quote: when deep encoding layers are employed within the data re-uploading model

equation:3.why: Repeated simple encoding gates set the accessible frequency spectrum, the role of S_l. It does not fix R_y.
equation:3.quote: By repeating simple data encoding gates multiple times, quantum models can access increasingly rich frequency spectra

equation:3.why: Data enter as nested qubit rotations with adjustable re-uploads, the rotation encoding with offset beta. It does not name R_y.
equation:3.quote: Considering a universal deep neural network organized as a series of nested qubit rotations, accomplished by adjustable data re-uploads

equation:4.why: Adds entanglement across several qubits to the re-uploading classifier, the V_ent factor. It does not name R_z R_y or CNOT.
equation:4.quote: The extension of this idea to several qubits enhances the efficiency of the strategy as entanglement expands the superpositions carried along with the classification

equation:4.why: Circuits with parameterized operations optimized classically, the trainable rotations of W_l.
equation:4.quote: circuits with parameterized operations that can be classically optimized in hybrid methods as variational quantum algorithms

equation:5.why: Ring-topology circuits reach the highest entanglement and expressibility, ahead of Linear, the closed CNOT ring of this equation.
equation:5.quote: circuits following a Ring topology will have the highest entanglement and expressibility values, followed by Linear/All-to-all almost together and the Star topology

equation:5.why: A more complex ansatz connectivity explores wider solution sets but adds gate overhead on hardware. It does not single out a ring.
equation:5.quote: a complex connectivity in the ansatz, albeit being beneficial for exploring wider sets of solutions, introduces an overhead of gates during the transpilation on a quantum computer

equation:6.why: Sends an initial state through a parametrized circuit and measures the expectation value of an operator, the quantity of this equation.
equation:6.quote: sending an initial state through a parametrized quantum circuit, and measuring the expectation value of some operator

equation:6.why: Costs built on local observables keep gradients at worst polynomially vanishing, the case of single-qubit Z_j.
equation:6.quote: defining C with local observables leads to at worst a polynomially vanishing gradient

equation:7.why: The objective of variational algorithms results from hybrid quantum-classical processing, of which this readout is a case.
equation:7.quote: the objective function is a result of hybrid quantum-classical processing

equation:7.why: Names local readouts of the individual qubits, the per-qubit inputs of this readout. It does not state the sigmoid.
equation:7.quote: compared to local readouts of the individual qubits in non-entangling networks

equation:8.why: Trains an ADHD EEG network with a regularized cross-entropy loss. Per-subject weights are this proposal's own.
equation:8.quote: a cross-entropy loss regularized through α-Rényi mutual information

equation:8.why: L2 regularization and weight decay coincide for standard SGD, the penalty on w and the decay on phi.
equation:8.quote: L$_2$ regularization and weight decay regularization are equivalent for standard stochastic gradient descent

equation:9.why: Visualizes a trained EEG network to interpret its learned features, a classical precedent. This channel-time formula is the proposal's own.
equation:9.quote: We demonstrate three different approaches to visualize the contents of a trained EEGNet model to enable interpretation of the learned features

equation:9.why: Computes the gradient of the class score with respect to the input, the classical origin of this map. Stated for images, not EEG.
equation:9.quote: We consider two visualisation techniques, based on computing the gradient of the class score with respect to the input image

equation:9.why: Gradients of expectation values come from running the circuit twice with one gate parameter shifted, the quantum factor. x_k enters L gates, so one pair per gate.
equation:9.quote: in many important instances it is sufficient to run the original quantum circuit twice while shifting a single gate parameter to obtain the corresponding component of the gradient

experiment:E1.why: Source of the EEGNet reference arm.
experiment:E1.quote: In this work we introduce EEGNet, a compact convolutional network for EEG-based BCIs

experiment:E1.why: Source of the ADHDeepNet reference arm, a temporal-spatial EEG model with attention modules.
experiment:E1.quote: We introduce ADHDeepNet, a DL model that utilizes comprehensive temporal-spatial characterization, attention modules, and explainability techniques optimized for EEG signals

experiment:E1.why: Out-of-the-box classical models outperform quantum classifiers overall, which justifies the classical controls.
experiment:E1.quote: We find that overall, out-of-the-box classical machine learning models outperform the quantum classifiers

experiment:E1.why: Precedent for strict subject-independent group partitions on ADHD EEG.
experiment:E1.quote: EEG-TACT was evaluated on a publicly available EEG dataset using strict, subject-independent stratified group partitions, ensuring that data from the same subject were never shared across the training, validation, and test subsets

experiment:E2.why: Removing entanglement often gives as good or better performance, so the ablation needs a separable arm.
experiment:E2.quote: removing entanglement from a quantum model often results in as good or better performance

experiment:E2.why: States that entanglement in the multi-qubit extension enhances the classifier's efficiency, the effect this ablation tests.
experiment:E2.quote: The extension of this idea to several qubits enhances the efficiency of the strategy as entanglement expands the superpositions carried along with the classification

experiment:E2.why: Ring-topology circuits reach higher entanglement and expressibility than Linear ones, the ring and linear arms of this ablation.
experiment:E2.quote: circuits following a Ring topology will have the highest entanglement and expressibility values, followed by Linear/All-to-all almost together and the Star topology

experiment:E2.why: Describes a four-qubit pure state whose average entanglement as two pairs appears maximal. The limit the protocol attributes to it rests on the full text, not ingested here.
experiment:E2.quote: We describe a pure state of four qubits whose single-qubit density matrices are all maximally mixed and whose average entanglement as a system of two pairs of qubits appears to be maximal

experiment:E3.why: Predictive performance of deep re-uploading models degrades toward random guessing as encoding layers increase; context for the depth sweep.
experiment:E3.quote: their predictive performance progressively degenerates to near random-guessing levels as the number of encoding layers increases

experiment:E3.why: Repeated encoding enlarges the accessible spectrum, the expressivity side of the depth trade-off.
experiment:E3.quote: By repeating simple data encoding gates multiple times, quantum models can access increasingly rich frequency spectra

experiment:E3.why: For a wide class of circuits a non-zero gradient at fixed precision is exponentially unlikely in the qubit count; its reach at 4 qubits is measured here.
experiment:E3.quote: for a wide class of reasonable parameterized quantum circuits, the probability that the gradient along any reasonable direction is non-zero to some fixed precision is exponentially small as a function of the number of qubits

experiment:E3.why: Iterative tuning of parameters lets a hybrid scheme circumvent high-depth circuits.
experiment:E3.quote: The iterative optimization of the parameters allows us to circumvent the high-depth circuit

experiment:E4.why: Precedent for visualizing a trained EEG network to interpret its learned features.
experiment:E4.quote: We demonstrate three different approaches to visualize the contents of a trained EEGNet model to enable interpretation of the learned features

experiment:E4.why: Precedent for identifying key brain regions and frequency bands from an ADHD EEG model.
experiment:E4.quote: To clarify model explainability and identify key brain regions and frequency bands for ADHD diagnosis, we analyzed the learned weights and activation patterns of the model's primary layers

experiment:E4.why: Visualizes a classifier from the gradient of the class score with respect to the input. Stated for images, not EEG.
experiment:E4.quote: We consider two visualisation techniques, based on computing the gradient of the class score with respect to the input image

experiment:E4.why: Gradients of expectation values come, in many instances, from two circuit runs with one gate parameter shifted.
experiment:E4.quote: in many important instances it is sufficient to run the original quantum circuit twice while shifting a single gate parameter to obtain the corresponding component of the gradient

experiment:E4.why: Excessive Theta/Beta ratio is not a reliable diagnostic measure of ADHD, which bounds how far a Theta/Beta contrast may be read.
experiment:E4.quote: Excessive TBR cannot be considered a reliable diagnostic measure of ADHD, however a substantial sub-group of ADHD patients do deviate on this measure

experiment:E5.why: The encoding gates determine the accessible frequencies, which predicts the frequency-two rule's outcome.
experiment:E5.quote: where the accessible frequencies are determined by the nature of the data encoding gates in the circuit

experiment:E5.why: Builds 160 datasets from 6 binary classification tasks to test models systematically, a precedent for a controlled benchmark.
experiment:E5.quote: systematically tests 12 popular quantum machine learning models on 6 binary classification tasks used to create 160 individual datasets

experiment:E5.why: Validates its re-uploading findings on synthetic linearly separable datasets as well as real data.
experiment:E5.quote: These findings are validated through experiments on both synthetic linearly separable datasets and real-world datasets

problem:central.why: On pediatric ADHD EEG, a model at 90.0% under segment-wise evaluation dropped to 65.6% under subject-wise evaluation.
problem:central.quote: However, the same model dropped to 65.6% (95% CI: [62.1%, 69.1%], AUC = 0.72) under subject-wise evaluation

problem:central.why: Quantum layers added to EEGNet give improvements that remain inconsistent across EEG datasets. It does not isolate shallow encodings.
problem:central.quote: while QEEGNet demonstrates competitive performance and maintains robustness in certain datasets, its improvements over traditional deep learning methods remain inconsistent

problem:central.why: States that robust subject-independent classification of ADHD from EEG remains challenging.
problem:central.quote: robust subject-independent classification remains challenging due to inter-subject variability, limited datasets, and the need for interpretable computational models

cause:DC1.why: Names low signal-to-noise ratio and high inter-subject variability, in infant EEG rather than ADHD.
cause:DC1.quote: Applying ML to infant data is particularly challenging due to the low number of trials, low signal-to-noise ratio, high inter-subject variability, and high inter-trial variability

cause:DC1.why: Names spatial blurring, low signal-to-noise ratio and inter-subject variability, in motor EEG decoding rather than ADHD.
cause:DC1.quote: Decoding motor intentions from non-invasive scalp EEG remains a core challenge in brain–computer interface research, due to spatial blurring, low signal-to-noise ratio, and inter-subject variability

cause:DC1.why: Attributes redundant spatiotemporal EEG features to volume conduction effects inherent to the human head.
cause:DC1.quote: which stem from the volume conduction effects inherent to the human head

cause:DC2.why: Reports novel constraints that limit the expressivity of parameterized quantum circuits.
cause:DC2.quote: These two behaviors imply novel forms of constraints which limit the expressivity of PQCs

cause:DC2.why: Bounds indicate that highly expressive ansatze exhibit flatter cost landscapes and are harder to train.
cause:DC2.quote: Our resulting bounds indicate that highly expressive ansatze exhibit flatter cost landscapes and therefore will be harder to train

cause:DC2.why: States that training variational circuits is hindered by barren plateaus, one source being circuit expressiveness.
cause:DC2.quote: the trainability of these algorithms is hindered by barren plateaus (BPs) induced by the expressiveness of the circuit

cause:DC3.why: Finds performance on previously-unseen subjects strongly overestimated under segment-based holdout.
cause:DC3.quote: we find that performance on previously-unseen subjects is strongly overestimated when models are trained using segment-based holdout

cause:DC3.why: Describes epochs of the same subject ending up in both training and testing sets, letting classifiers use individual-specific features.
cause:DC3.quote: whereby EEG epochs pertaining to the same subject end up in both training and testing sets, allowing classifiers to capitalize on features specific to the individual rather than on genuine disorder-related biomarkers
